fr.title: Animateur emblématique des « Grosses têtes », Philippe Bouvard est mort à l’âge de 96 ans
fr.description: Lecture zen L’animateur des « Grosses têtes », Philippe Bouvard est photographié, le 29 mars 2010, dans les studios de la radio RTL à Paris, lors de l’enregistrement de son émission. - AFP Plume acérée et verbe haut, Philippe Bouvard était une figure historique du monde des médias français. Animateur historique de l’émission Les Grosses têtes sur RTL, le journaliste est mort à l’âge de 96 ans à son domicile de Cannes, ce lundi 24 août 2026. Lui qui avait fait ses premières armes dans la presse écrite n’a cessé, au fil de sa carrière, de toucher à tous les métiers nécessitant de manier les mots : auteur de théâtre, dialoguiste de cinéma. Révélateur d’humoristes La radio dont il était l’un des grands noms, RTL , le décrit comme un « amuseur indompté ». Il fut le premier animateur des Grosses Têtes en 1977 puis aux commandes de l’émission de télévision Le Théâtre de Bouvard sur Antenne 2, qui a révélé toute une génération d’humoristes parmi lesquels Muriel Robin, Pascal Légitimus, Mimie Mathy ou encore Chevallier et Laspalès... Après 37 ans à animer les « Grosses têtes », Philippe Bouvard avait laissé sa place à contrecœur en 2014 à Laurent Ruquier, appelé pour rajeunir l’émission. 60 ans de carrière Immédiatement reconnaissable à son visage rond et son œil malicieux, Philippe Bouvard disait incarner les qualités et les défauts du Français moyen. En janvier 2019, dans Paris Match, il confiait se regarder vieillir « avec curiosité », convaincu que « la vie vaut d’être vécue jusqu’au bout ». Philippe Bouvard a toujours été un hyperactif : 30.000 articles, 6.000 émissions de télé, recensait-il début 2013 dans le quotidien Nice-Matin auquel il a collaboré. Le journaliste avait d’ailleurs pris officiellement sa retraite en janvier 2025, après 60 ans de carrière. « Notre maître à tous » Membre de l’équipe des Grosses Têtes Bernard Mabille salue la mémoire de Philippe Bouvard sur RTL. « C’était quelqu’un de curieusement très attachant. Je n’ai jamais su s’il nous aimait ou pas » Pour Jean-Pierre Foucault , autre grand nom de la télévision et de la radio, c’était « notre maître à tous » : « Philippe a su mettre à la portée de tous la culture générale, il était doté d’une immense culture et c’était la porte ouverte à la culture générale, au rire, à l’humour, à la dérision, à l’autodérision. » Pour Laurent Ruquier , qui a pris sa suite aux commandes de l’émission culte, « Même Coluche sur Europe 1 n’a jamais détrôné les Grosses Têtes de Philippe Bouvard ! ». L’animateur s’est dit « très fier d’avoir continué à faire vivre ce bébé. » Mis en ligne le 24/08/2026 à 09:19 Animateur emblématique des « Grosses têtes », Philippe Bouvard est mort à l’âge de 96 ans Par Stéphanie Verger Journaliste et animateur vedette sur RTL, Philippe Bouvard a marqué l’histoire de la télévision et de la radio française.

es.title: Laura Martínez y Agustín Siancha, campeones del XXII Open Tenis de la Amistad de Almuñécar
es.description: El XXII Open Tenis de la Amistad de Almuñécar 2026 - Memorial Diego Fernández ya tiene campeones. Laura Martínez y Agustín Siancha se proclamaron vencedores de una edición que del 17 al 22 de agosto reunió a más de medio centenar de tenistas en las pistas del Complejo Deportivo Municipal ‘Río Verde’. El evento destacó por el gran nivel de juego y la afluencia de público. En la final del cuadro femenino Laura Martínez se impuso, de forma contundente, a Lucía Hickey por 6-2 y 6-0. La jugadora murciana, que ya conquistó este torneo en 2024, suma así su segundo triunfo en el Open en su segunda participación. En la competición masculina el malagueño Agustín Siancha, de tan solo 16 años, se proclamó campeón tras superar a Pablo Hermoso por 6-2 y 6-2. Como parte de la jornada final se celebró además un set de exhibición de la mano de Quino Muñoz, exjugador ATP y actual director del circuito IBP Tenis, y Fabián Núñez Seixa, fundador y director de TE-MA Tennis Management. La tradicional entrega de premios estuvo presidida por Luis Aragón, concejal de Deportes del Ayuntamiento de Almuñécar; junto a Carmen Castillo Guarnido, presidenta del Club de Tenis Costa Tropical; y María Dolores Ruiz Martín, en representación de la organización. Hay que recordar que el XXII Open Tenis de la Amistad de Almuñécar 2026 - Memorial Diego Fernández forma parte del Circuito Nacional IBP Tenis Series y cuenta con la colaboración del Área Municipal de Deportes de Almuñécar y la Federación Andaluza de Tenis. En el acto el edil Luis Aragón destacó “el enorme trabajo que realiza todo el equipo del Club de Tenis Costa Tropical para que este Open siga creciendo. También quiero agradecer a todos los participantes su confianza y animarles a volver el próximo año. Esperamos que hayan disfrutado de la competición y de Almuñécar, porque nuestro objetivo es que este torneo siga creciendo y tenga cada vez mayor proyección”, señaló. Por su parte, María Dolores Ruiz Martín destacó “el altísimo nivel de los jugadores y el gran ambiente que se ha vivido durante toda la semana”; a la vez que agradeció la implicación del Área de Deportes del ayuntamiento sexitano, así como a patrocinadores, colaboradores, jueces y todas las personas que han hecho posible el torneo.

mx.title: Esta nueva amenaza de Android se aprovecha de los permisos de la VPN
mx.description: Una nueva amenaza de seguridad puede comprometer los dispositivos con Android. Se trata de ToxicPanda , un malware detectado recientemente por investigadores de seguridad de Zimperium . Se aprovecha de los permisos de VPN y puede bloquear Google Play . Tiene múltiples funcionalidades que pueden afectar al buen funcionamiento de tus dispositivos sin que seas consciente de ello. El malware solicita permisos de VPN Según explican los investigadores de seguridad, este malware tiene ahora la capacidad de solicitar permisos del servicio VPN y así crear una interfaz local que permita controlar el tráfico de red que pasa a través de ella. Esto es lo que le permite bloquear la comunicación con Google Play y los Servicios de Google Play. Esto es un problema importante, ya que el control a nivel de red permite al malware ToxicPanda 2.0 interferir en las comprobaciones y acciones de seguridad . Estas comprobaciones incluyen verificaciones de aplicaciones, también actualizaciones, comunicaciones de Google Protect e interrupciones legítimas diseñadas para proteger a los usuarios. Cuando obtiene los permisos del servicio VPN, ToxicPanda 2.0 bloquea las comunicaciones con Google Play. A partir de ahí es cuando empieza a extraer e instalar la carga útil y solicita permisos de Accesibilidad . Los informes de Zimperium, de los cuales se han hecho eco medios como Bleeping Computer , indican que se está distribuyendo a través de buckets alojados en Amazon AWS . La última versión del malware admite 167 comandos remotos y superposiciones de phishing para 349 aplicaciones bancarias, financieras, de criptomonedas y monederos electrónicos. Afecta a 16 países, según indican desde Zimperium. Estas superposiciones de phishing son invisibles para la víctima. Creen que están poniendo la contraseña en la aplicación bancaria legítima, pero realmente están entregando esas credenciales a los piratas informáticos. Además, ToxicPanda puede falsificar la pantalla de bloqueo y robar así el PIN, patrones de desbloqueos y contraseñas que ponga la víctima. En definitiva, ToxicPanda se aprovecha de una VPN legítima, de crear un túnel para proteger o redirigir el tráfico, y así intervenir en el dispositivo.

ph.title: Eala also needs to lose to rest
ph.description: There’s a time when losing is actually good for an athlete, maybe except in boxing. The same applies to Alex Eala, who lost to WTA World No. 10 Amanda Anisimova at the Cincinnati Open in three sets. While there were tennis fans who felt a letdown on Eala losing to Anisimova, there were those who felt relieved because Eala badly needed rest for the US Open and the successive WTA rounds in Asia as the year closes. Eala now has a 37-19 win-loss record this year, and that’s a total of 56 matches. That is among the highest for female tennis players. Also, Eala had to battle top-notch players such as Iga Swiatek, Elena Rybakina, Elina Svitolina (twice), Jessica Pegula, and Naomi Osaka who are all certified tennis royalty. On the other hand, a surging Sara Bejlek from the Czech Republic has a 22-14 win-loss record, figuring in 36 matches. That’s 20 less matches compared to Eala. Make no mistake – I admire Bejlek because with her petite frame, she proves that size not a might in tennis. Just see what she did to WTA No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka at Cincinnati. Bejlek and Jasmine Paolini (yes, I admire her too) clearly show that tennis is also for Filipinos. Bejlek making waves at Cincinnati shows rest is important for an athlete, even for the young ones. The Czech is only 20 years old. I mean, imagine if Eala had 10, 15 or 20 less matches at this point? But then, Eala’s quandary now is she is among the “darlings” in the global tennis world. And it seems that she will not run out of opportunities to figure in major WTA tournaments, including the Grand Slams. In fact, if I were a tennis event organizer and the one putting down the money, I would go to war to get Eala into the line up because she draws crowds at the gate, and eyeballs over social media. And those are what matter to sponsors, especially big-name sponsors. Have you seen how the lead organizers or representatives of the recent tennis events Eala figured in smile ear-to-ear or are very happy when interviewed? That’s the Eala impact. Eala also deserves more respect because a sports figure competing before crowd wildly cheering him or her puts tons of pressures on the athlete. And I mean tons of pressure, because Eala has to at least please the crowd, even if she is drained or injured. How many times have we witnessed that? In boxing, there are excellent examples of athletes who thrive even with a maddening crowd, such us our very own Manny Pacquiao, Mexico’s Canelo Alvarez, and Tyson Fury of the United Kingdom. But in boxing, the top guns have the time to “rest” because they have the leverage to dictate when they will fight anew, and even “choose” their opponent. Ask Floyd Mayweather Jr. Even “aspiring” fighters in boxing also have the luxury of taking time off, especially if their promoters are powerful enough to influence the sanctioning bodies. In tennis, those are completely impossible as the WTA gives “obligations” to players, most especially those climbing to the top like Eala, to participate in high-level tournaments. I can also imagine how taxing it is for Eala and other tennis players to participate in singles and doubles matches in a certain tournament, because they have to fulfill an “obligation.” So, when Eala loses, let us look at the positive side of that, which is the chance for her to take a much-needed rest. And definitely, we want to see Eala well-rested and sharply-focused in the next matches to come, so she can hoist more trophies.

bd.title: ImmunoForge Selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups' 'Global TIPS R&D' Program... "Expansion of the LMT Platform"
bd.description: Development of Leptin receptor-based technology and hybrid LNP platform Combining Blood-Brain Barrier penetration and a one-month sustained-release formulation in a single structure, with potential applications in CNS-targeted therapeutics Technology validated by winning first place in Novo Nordisk's Open Innovation contest... Accelerating global technology transfer SEOUL, South Korea , Aug. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ImmunoForge (Co-CEOs Sung-Min Ahn and Ki-Ho Chang), a biotech venture specializing in the development of therapeutics for rare diseases, announced that it has been finally selected for the 2026 Investment and Financing-Linked Technology Development Program (Global TIPS R&D), organized by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS) and the Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs (TIPA). The program selected promising global companies in the domestic biotechnology and healthcare sectors through a two-stage evaluation process consisting of a first-round written evaluation and a second-round in-person evaluation. As a final selected company, ImmunoForge will receive a total of KRW 5 billion in government funding over the next four years. The LMT (Leptin receptor-Mediated Transcytosis) platform, which received particular attention in this project, is based on Leptin receptor-mediated transcytosis technology. Compared with existing Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) penetration technologies, it has clear advantages, including lower side effects and higher permeability. BBB Penetration and One-Month Sustained-Release Formulation... Building a Differentiated CNS Platform In particular, ImmunoForge has fused its proprietary long-acting technology, ELP, with the LMT platform to implement BBB penetration and one-month sustained release in a single structure. This is expected to enable applications in various areas, including CNS-targeted therapeutics with a one-month formulation. In addition, the BBB-penetrating LNP platform being developed through this project is a hybrid platform that combines Leptin receptor-mediated transcytosis technology with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). The goal is to establish a hybrid platform that directly targets the central nervous system and to complete the development process through the preclinical stage. Building on its selection for this project, ImmunoForge plans to move forward with full-scale development by combining its BBB delivery technology with CNS-targeted drug candidates based on the company's platform technologies. pk.title: Fils claims first ATP Masters 1000 title as Gauff clinches second Cincinnati crown
pk.description: CINCINNATI: Arthur Fils defeated Frances Tiafoe to secure his first ATP Masters 1000 title on Sunday, while Coco Gauff beat Jessica Pegula to win her second Cincinnati Open title. Fils bounced back from a second-set wobble to beat American Tiafoe 6-3 1-6 6-0. The 21st seed made a flying start by breaking early to establish a 3-0 lead in the opening set before Tiafoe got on the board with a hold of serve. The Frenchman maintained relentless pressure from the baseline, attacking Tiafoe’s second serve and forcing errors as he moved 5-3 ahead. Fils was untouchable on serve, closing out the set with three successive aces without dropping a point in the final game. Tiafoe, playing in his second Cincinnati final, responded in kind in the second set. The 28-year-old broke in the second game en route to a 3-0 lead, with his forehands pulling Fils wide. Although Fils got on the board with a hold to love, the 17th seed Tiafoe broke again for a 5-1 advantage before forcing a decider. Fils quickly regained control in the third set, breaking twice to race to a 4-0 lead as Tiafoe’s backhand errors piled up. The 22-year-old’s pace proved too much for the American, and he closed out the match with a 6-0 final set after a lengthy rally to lift the Cincinnati trophy. “It was tough, because I started very, very strong, and then in the second set I lost a little bit of focus,” Fils said. “To be able to win one title like this means a lot to me...It’s a lot of training, a lot of things, a lot of sacrifice,” he added. Gauff secured her second Cincinnati title in the women’s final, defeating world number three Pegula in a dominant 6-2 6-4 victory. The 22-year-old American quickly established a 5-0 lead in the opening set, breaking twice and capitalising on her compatriot’s double faults. Pegula, who ousted defending champion Iga Swiatek on Saturday, broke Gauff without dropping a point at 5-2 but was unable to recover from the early deficit against the power of the world number four’s forehand. Gauff powers past Pegula to win US Open warm-up in Cincinnati Gauff, building momentum ahead of the US Open, rapidly took a 3-0 lead in the second set, breaking in the second game while taking advantage of the 32-year-old’s failed returns. Pegula, who lost the Washington Open final to Alexandra Eala earlier this month, held to love in the seventh game before breaking serve to reduce the deficit to 5-4. However the two-time Grand Slam champion Gauff broke back to close the set to love and clinch her 12th career singles title.

pk.title: Australia's bowlers restore order but batting headaches remain ahead of South Africa tour
pk.description: MELBOURNE: Normal service resumed for Australia as their formidable bowling unit hit their marks in the second test against Bangladesh in Mackay but questions remain over a batting order that continues to misfire at the top. Australia’s innings and 51-run victory was a strong comeback from the Darwin defeat as pace leaders Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins blasted away the tourists’ batters in a timely reminder of their quality ahead of a tough, three-test tour of South Africa in October. Australia’s batting has left selectors with a headache, though, and struggling number three Marnus Labuschagne may be nervous about his place in the squad for South Africa. South Africa-born Labuschagne was already under major scrutiny after two poor dismissals in Darwin before he was bowled for four in Mackay by Shoriful Islam, the ball catching his thigh pad before hitting the stumps. Upon his dismissal, Labuschagne gave the look of a man forsaken by the cricketing gods and later took scissors to his thigh pad in an unusual gear modification. But behind the theatrics was a batter who had strayed far across his crease and given Shoriful a look at leg stump, further evidence for pundits of a need for change. “There’s some technical deficiency there, but he’s making the margin for error for the bowlers too great,” said former Australia captain Ricky Ponting. “It’s well and truly time to have a look at somebody else.” Labuschagne’s exit would be the second top-order batter dropped in two matches after opener Jake Weatherald was dumped in the wake of the fiasco in Darwin, where Australia fell to a shock nine-wicket defeat. Weatherald’s replacement Matt Renshaw hardly inspired in his first test in over three years, falling for eight with a nick to the slips, but he will be afforded time to bed into the role. Whether Travis Head should accompany him at the top of the order remains a troublesome question for selectors. Moved up from the middle order for the Ashes as Usman Khawaja struggled with injury, Head has remained there despite not really being seen as a proper opener. Some former players, including Mark Waugh, want Head back down in the middle order but that would mean gambling with two unproven openers against South Africa, who beat Australia for the World Test Championship title last year. With runs in Darwin and Mackay, Cameron Green has belatedly shored up his spot at number five so bringing Head back down would mean upsetting the formula of having wicketkeeper Alex Carey at six and the second all-rounder Beau Webster at seven. Selectors picked a thin 13-man squad for the Bangladesh series but are expected to take at least 16 to South Africa and include additional batting cover. Australia thrash Bangladesh by innings and 51 runs in Mackay to tie series Quite who gets the nod among the batters on the fringes is far from certain, with no real stand-out candidates having emerged. Carey said there was no urgency to shake up Australia’s batting lineup further. “I think we felt a little bit like we left some runs out there (against Bangladesh), so we are always looking to improve as a batting unit,” he told reporters in Mackay. “We are hungry. We are working really hard.”

pk.title: In Afghanistan, cash assistance is rebuilding lives and supporting resilience against future extremes | IFRC
pk.description: Country: Afghanistan Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies In late May 2026, heavy rainfall triggered devastating flash floods across several provinces in northern and north-eastern Afghanistan. Entire communities were caught off guard as torrents of water surged through villages, sweeping away household belongings, destroying crops, damaging homes, and disrupting livelihoods. The floods struck just days before Eid al-Adha, one of the most important celebrations of the year. Instead of preparing for family gatherings and festivities, thousands of families found themselves struggling to protect their homes and salvage what little remained. On the outskirts of Kunduz city, Zahra (pseudonym), a mother of two, still remembers the night the floodwaters arrived. “There was no warning. We were sleeping and when we woke up, the house was flooded.” Within hours, the family's food stocks, kitchen utensils, household possessions and supplies prepared for Eid had disappeared beneath muddy water. “We were busy preparing for Eid, but the flood came and took everything away,” Zahra recalls. The family's yard was completely submerged, while the thick mud walls of their home were left deeply cracked by the force of the floodwaters. More than two months later, they still worry the damaged structure could collapse at any time. Rather than celebrating Eid, Zahra's children spent the holiday helping their parents clean up the aftermath. Together, they gathered what could be recovered, washing, repairing and restoring anything the flood had spared. “It wasn't just us; the entire village was affected,” she adds. Afghan Red Crescent Society teams engage with communities affected by flooding in Afghanistan. Through emergency response and recovery support, the National Society helps families cope with the impacts of recurrent climate- and weather-related disasters. Photo: Afghan Red Crescent Society The challenges remain even after the waters recede For families in Kunduz, the flood's impact did not end when the water disappeared. Overflowing sewage mixed with the floodwaters that swept through homes and neighbourhoods. In the weeks that followed, many children developed skin rashes and sores, while diarrhoeal illness became common across affected communities. The financial burden has also been immense for families already living on the edge of poverty. Zahra's husband works as a day labourer, earning around 350 AFN (approximately US$5) per day when work is available. With unemployment high, he is often able to find work for only around ten days each month, leaving the family with a monthly income of roughly US$50. Faced with repairing a damaged home and replacing essential belongings, the road to recovery felt daunting. “I pray we don't face this kind of situation again. This time we were lucky, but next time, who knows what could happen? If one of the children had been hurt or worse, I don't know what we would have done,” says Zahra. Support to help families rebuild As communities slowly begin to recover, the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) , with support from the IFRC and the British Red Cross, is helping families meet some of their most urgent recovery needs through cash assistance. Cash assistance is one of the most effective forms of support following sudden disasters, particularly in areas where local markets remain functional. It allows families to decide for themselves what they need most. For some households, the priority is repairing homes. For others, especially farming families, it means buying seeds, fertiliser or tools to restore their livelihoods. On the day she met with Red Crescent teams, Zahra collected 10,500 AFN (approximately US$160) as part of the emergency cash assistance programme. For her family, the money will go towards purchasing materials to begin repairing their damaged home. “The money I collected today is a very useful start, but we still have a long way to go,” she says. Zahra's family is one of 250 households in Kunduz city and another 150 households in Badakhshan province's Tagab district receiving cash assistance. Fifty of the families supported in Kunduz are female-headed households. Priority has been given to families whose homes were partially or completely damaged by the floods. Cash assistance gives families the flexibility to prioritise their own recovery needs. For people affected by the floods in northern Afghanistan, the support can help repair damaged homes, replace essential belongings or restore livelihoods. Photo: IFRC A recovery that extends beyond today While cash assistance is helping families take their first steps towards recovery, rebuilding livelihoods and strengthening resilience will take much longer. Known as Afghanistan's "granary" because of its rich agricultural production, Kunduz was among the areas hardest hit by the floods. Around 6,500 acres of farmland were damaged and more than 2,000 families affected. Many households lost harvested crops and seed reserves intended for the next planting season. According to Muhammad Raza Naseri, Director of the Afghan Red Crescent Society’s Kunduz Branch , communities are increasingly aware that extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and unpredictable. “You won't hear anyone from here using the term climate change, but they know it is happening because they are living it,” Naseri says. “We know the periods of drought are getting worse, we know the water levels in our springs are reducing, we know we are getting rains and floods at different times of year than before, and we know we are experiencing extreme heat every year now. We have noticed all these things because our lives and our livelihoods depend on them.” As immediate needs begin to stabilise, communities and humanitarian partners alike recognise that recovery must go beyond repairing damaged homes. Restoring livelihoods and helping families prepare for future shocks are equally important. Shaimaa Jarrar, IFRC Operations Manager in Afghanistan , emphasises the need for sustained investment in resilience and preparedness. “Afghanistan is one of the countries in the world most vulnerable to climate change. Extreme weather like floods and droughts, combined with the effects of ongoing poverty and decades of conflict, intensify the impact on communities across the country,” Jarrar says. “It is critical that, as well as responding to acute emergency needs, we also help communities better prepare for future shocks, increasing resilience and reducing vulnerability for the long term,” she adds. For families like Zahra's, the floodwaters may have receded, but recovery continues every day. Rebuilding homes, restoring livelihoods and regaining a sense of security will take time. The cash assistance they have received is an important first step, while longer-term support will help communities better withstand the increasingly frequent and severe weather extremes they face. -- Learn more about how cash and voucher assistance helps people affected by disasters recover with dignity and choice.

ae.title: ImmunoForge Selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups' 'Global TIPS R&D' Program... "Expansion of the LMT Platform"
ae.description: Development of Leptin receptor-based technology and hybrid LNP platform Combining Blood-Brain Barrier penetration and a one-month sustained-release formulation in a single structure, with potential applications in CNS-targeted therapeutics Technology validated by winning first place in Novo Nordisk's Open Innovation contest... Accelerating global technology transfer SEOUL, South Korea , Aug. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ImmunoForge (Co-CEOs Sung-Min Ahn and Ki-Ho Chang), a biotech venture specializing in the development of therapeutics for rare diseases, announced that it has been finally selected for the 2026 Investment and Financing-Linked Technology Development Program (Global TIPS R&D), organized by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS) and the Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs (TIPA). The program selected promising global companies in the domestic biotechnology and healthcare sectors through a two-stage evaluation process consisting of a first-round written evaluation and a second-round in-person evaluation. As a final selected company, ImmunoForge will receive a total of KRW 5 billion in government funding over the next four years. The LMT (Leptin receptor-Mediated Transcytosis) platform, which received particular attention in this project, is based on Leptin receptor-mediated transcytosis technology. Compared with existing Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) penetration technologies, it has clear advantages, including lower side effects and higher permeability. BBB Penetration and One-Month Sustained-Release Formulation... Building a Differentiated CNS Platform In particular, ImmunoForge has fused its proprietary long-acting technology, ELP, with the LMT platform to implement BBB penetration and one-month sustained release in a single structure. This is expected to enable applications in various areas, including CNS-targeted therapeutics with a one-month formulation. In addition, the BBB-penetrating LNP platform being developed through this project is a hybrid platform that combines Leptin receptor-mediated transcytosis technology with lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). The goal is to establish a hybrid platform that directly targets the central nervous system and to complete the development process through the preclinical stage. Building on its selection for this project, ImmunoForge plans to move forward with full-scale development by combining its BBB delivery technology with CNS-targeted drug candidates based on the company's platform technologies. Global Partnerships to Accelerate Ki-Ho Chang, Co-CEO of ImmunoForge, said, "Through our selection for the Global TIPS R&D program, we plan to further advance the LMT platform and develop new drug peptides with various domestic and international companies." He added, "In addition, we plan to pursue collaborative research and co-development to identify CNS-targeted drug candidates by utilizing LNP technologies with various modalities, including mRNA, siRNA, and ASO. We are already receiving interest from global companies and are currently discussing collaborative research with multiple companies." "We will also actively pursue global technology transfer with global companies based on our differentiated technologies," Chang added. Sung-Min Ahn, Co-CEO of ImmunoForge, said, "The fact that our technology won first place in the Open Innovation contest hosted by global pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk is evidence that our technological capabilities have been recognized at a global level." "We will continue to expand our technologies so that we can become a key partner for global companies in the field of central nervous system disorders," Ahn emphasized. [Project Overview] Project Title: Development and Preclinical Validation of an Innovative Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)-Penetrating Hybrid LNP Platform (Global TIPS R&D) Project Funding: A total of KRW 5 billion over four years (entirely government-funded) Host Organization: Ministry of SMEs and Startups (MSS) / Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs (TIPA)

sa.title: 26 ألف طالب وطالبة.. جامعة جدة تبدأ العام الجامعي بخدمات رقمية
sa.description:
استقبلت جامعة جدة أكثر من 26 ألف طالب وطالبة للعام الجامعي 1448هـ، معتمدة على منظومة إلكترونية متكاملة لتسهيل الخدمات التعليمية والإجراءات التنظيمية، وتسريع انتظامهم في مقاعد الدراسة.

وأكد رئيس الجامعة الدكتور عبيد آل مظف، أن الطلبة المقبولين يمثلون محور رحلة الجامعة الأكاديمية وغايتها الأساسية. وأوضح أن ما تقدمه المنظومة الجامعية من معرفة ومهارات وتجارب متنوعة، يمثل استثماراً حقيقياً في صناعة قادة المستقبل وصناع الأثر.

ووجه آل مظف حديثه للطلبة الجدد قائلاً: «أنتم أمل الوطن وقادة مستقبله، وعليكم مسؤولية كبيرة تجاه دينكم ووطنكم». وأشار إلى أن الجهات المعنية داخل الجامعة عملت على ضمان انطلاقة دراسية منظمة تواكب تطلعات المستفيدين.

خدمات مبتكرة لراحة الطلاب

وكشف رئيس الجامعة عن توفير حزمة من الخدمات الرقمية المبتكرة التي تستهدف تعزيز راحة الطلبة وتحسين جودة تجربتهم الأكاديمية. وبيّن أن الإجراءات التنظيمية تضمنت تفعيل الخرائط الإلكترونية التفاعلية داخل الحرم الجامعي لتسهيل وصول الطلبة إلى مرافقهم.

وأضاف أن الجامعة أتاحت خدمة إصدار البطاقات الجامعية رقمياً عبر تطبيق «جامعة جدة UJ CONNECT». ولفت إلى أن هذا التطبيق يتيح للطلبة استعراض الجداول الدراسية ومواعيد المحاضرات بكل سهولة، مما يسهم في الارتقاء بجودة الحياة الجامعية وتعزيز كفاءة العملية التعليمية.

iq.title: اتحاد الملاكمة يعلن إقامة بطولة الأندية للناشئين والأشبال في السليمانية
iq.description: شفق نيوز- السليمانية أعلن الاتحاد العراقي للملاكمة، يوم الاثنين،إقامة بطولة الأندية العراقية لفئتي الناشئين والأشبال في محافظة السليمانية، خلالشهر أيلول/سبتمبر المقبل، بمشاركة واسعة متوقعة من ملاكمي الأندية من مختلفالمحافظات والأوزان. وقال رئيس الاتحاد العراقي للملاكمةعلي تكليف لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن "البطولة ستنطلق في السليمانية وستشهد مشاركةعدد كبير من الملاكمين الذين يمثلون أندية من مختلف محافظات العراق"، مبيناًأن "المنافسات ستقام بمشاركة مختلف الأوزان المعتمدة للفئتين". وأضاف تكليف أن "الاتحاد يوليبطولات الفئات العمرية أهمية كبيرة ضمن برنامجه وخطته لتطوير اللعبة"، مؤكداًأن "هذه البطولات تمثل إحدى الركائز الأساسية لاكتشاف المواهب وصقلهاوإعدادها بالشكل الصحيح، وصولاً إلى رفد المنتخبات الوطنية بملاكمين قادرين علىتمثيل العراق في الاستحقاقات والمحافل الدولية خلال السنوات المقبلة". وأوضح أن البطولة تأتي ضمن سلسلةالنشاطات والمسابقات التي ينظمها الاتحاد ضمن منهاجه لتنشيط المنافسات المحليةوالارتقاء بالمستوى الفني للملاكمين، إلى جانب إعداد جيل جديد قادر على مواصلةحضور الملاكمة العراقية في البطولات العربية والقارية والدولية. وأشار إلى أن إقامة بطولة الأندية فيالسليمانية "تسهم في تعزيز التواصل بين أندية المحافظات العراقية، وفتحالمجال أمام اكتشاف عدد من المواهب الواعدة التي يمكن أن تشكل نواة للمنتخباتالوطنية في المستقبل". وأشاد تكليف بدور اللجنة الأولمبيةالعراقية في دعم الاتحاد مادياً ومعنوياً، لافتاً إلى أن الاتحاد "يعانيضائقة مالية بسبب عدم صرف مستحقاته منذ ثلاث سنوات".

na.title: Death toll rises to 30 in Guinea rubbish dump landslide
na.description:
Conakry: A landslide at the Dar-es-Salam rubbish dump on the outskirts of Conakry, the Guinean capital, on Sunday has killed 30 people and injured 22 others, according to a statement issued by the Guinean government.

"Since the early hours, significant human and material resources have been mobilized to search for any people who may still be buried, rescue victims and recover bodies," the statement said.

According to the statement, operations are continuing on the ground under the coordination of the relevant state services, with the support of the Red Cross, the defense and security forces, medical teams, administrative and local authorities, as well as residents of surrounding areas.

Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah visited the site to assess the situation and oversee the mobilization of public services, the statement said.

Bah, on behalf of President Mamady Doumbouya, expressed his deep sympathy and the government's solidarity with the bereaved families.

"All necessary measures have been taken to ensure medical care for the injured, particularly at Donka National Hospital, as well as assistance to people affected by the disaster," said the prime minister.

Bah called on the public to remain calm, show solidarity and strictly follow instructions from rescue services and the relevant authorities.

zm.title: Death toll rises to 30 in Guinea rubbish dump landslide
zm.description:
Conakry: A landslide at the Dar-es-Salam rubbish dump on the outskirts of Conakry, the Guinean capital, on Sunday has killed 30 people and injured 22 others, according to a statement issued by the Guinean government.

"Since the early hours, significant human and material resources have been mobilized to search for any people who may still be buried, rescue victims and recover bodies," the statement said.

According to the statement, operations are continuing on the ground under the coordination of the relevant state services, with the support of the Red Cross, the defense and security forces, medical teams, administrative and local authorities, as well as residents of surrounding areas.

Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah visited the site to assess the situation and oversee the mobilization of public services, the statement said.

Bah, on behalf of President Mamady Doumbouya, expressed his deep sympathy and the government's solidarity with the bereaved families.

"All necessary measures have been taken to ensure medical care for the injured, particularly at Donka National Hospital, as well as assistance to people affected by the disaster," said the prime minister.

Bah called on the public to remain calm, show solidarity and strictly follow instructions from rescue services and the relevant authorities.

bw.title: Death toll rises to 30 in Guinea rubbish dump landslide
bw.description:
Conakry: A landslide at the Dar-es-Salam rubbish dump on the outskirts of Conakry, the Guinean capital, on Sunday has killed 30 people and injured 22 others, according to a statement issued by the Guinean government.

"Since the early hours, significant human and material resources have been mobilized to search for any people who may still be buried, rescue victims and recover bodies," the statement said.

According to the statement, operations are continuing on the ground under the coordination of the relevant state services, with the support of the Red Cross, the defense and security forces, medical teams, administrative and local authorities, as well as residents of surrounding areas.

Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah visited the site to assess the situation and oversee the mobilization of public services, the statement said.

Bah, on behalf of President Mamady Doumbouya, expressed his deep sympathy and the government's solidarity with the bereaved families.

"All necessary measures have been taken to ensure medical care for the injured, particularly at Donka National Hospital, as well as assistance to people affected by the disaster," said the prime minister.

Bah called on the public to remain calm, show solidarity and strictly follow instructions from rescue services and the relevant authorities.
